key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni-20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% relative to bare SA516 boiler steel, outperforming the other tested coatings.
engineering_relevance: This coating is a promising option for improving SA516 boiler steel resistance to high-temperature oxidation.
method: Apply Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN coatings using HVOF and plasma spraying.
Characterize phases and microstructure using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: Laboratory testing linked the best oxidation performance to a dense protective oxide layer containing Cr2O3, TiO2, NiTiO4, and NiO, alongside reduced porosity and enhanced microhardness.
watch_item: Performance over 50 laboratory air-oxidation cycles does not establish long-term durability in corrosive boiler-service environments.
paper_title: Microstructure and high-temperature oxidation behaviour of HVOF and plasma sprayed Ni–Cr-based ceramic coatings on SA516 boiler steel
